issues.detail: The skill is centred on NVIDIA GPUs and CUDA (nvidia runtime, nvidia-smi, CUDA 12.8 for Blackwell), and gives no commands for the AMD ROCm, TPU or CPU builds that the compatibility line mentions.

scenarios.name: serve-70b-multi-gpu-team
scenarios.rationale: Response A covers every rubric item: `vllm serve`, TP 4, served name, API key, HF_TOKEN with the licence note, and `--host 127.0.0.1` with a TLS gateway in front. Response B covers the core flags and mentions the gated model and a TLS proxy, but its commands expose the port publicly with `-p 8000:8000` and `--host 0.0.0.0`, and it only suggests firewalling afterwards.

scenarios.name: fix-startup-oom-on-4090
scenarios.rationale: B hits every rubric item: the model can't fit in 24 GB, use the pre-quantized AWQ checkpoint, set --max-model-len 8192, say vLLM won't quantize on the fly, and check nvidia-smi. A recommends the AWQ checkpoint and lower max-model-len, but it passes --quantization awq_marlin and offers on-the-fly FP8 as if it solves the OOM, which the rubric warns against, and it puts nvidia-smi only as a secondary note.

scenarios.name: docker-vllm-with-embeddings-client
scenarios.rationale: A hits the rubric's key details: `--runtime nvidia --gpus all`, `--ipc=host`, a mounted HF cache, a 127.0.0.1-bound port mapping, model args after the image, and a separate server on its own port for embeddings with `embeddings.create` on the `/v1` base_url. B omits `--runtime nvidia` and binds ports to all interfaces (`-p 8000:8000`), which breaks the localhost-binding requirement, though it does serve embeddings separately and uses the SDK correctly.
